Alicia (runtime): Heads-up: Support ticket #5872 — customer reported sudden p95/p99 latency regressions in us-east-1 for text-generation endpoints starting ~08:15 UTC. p95 jumped from ~180ms to 1.2s, p99 to ~2.5s. No error codes, just slow responses.

Mike H: Seen that in metrics — KV/prefix cache miss rate spiked at the same time. Eviction rate went up 3x, and we saw a burst of new prefix keys. Looks like a key-entropy burst (many unique prefixes).

Sean L: Any deploys or config changes around 08:00-08:10?

DeployBot: deploy redwood-runtime v2.14.3 to us-east-1 finished at 07:58 UTC (canary -> region).

Alicia (runtime): There was a canary earlier. But the p95 jump aligns with customer traffic pattern — bigger batched prompts with user-supplied metadata header. Suspect header-derived prefix keys not normalized -> cardinality explosion.

Luis Ops: I pulled host logs. We see repeated cache-key collisions and then immediate evictions. Sample log: 
```
[kvcache] miss key=prefix:UserMeta:session=abc123:locale=en-US:ua=Mozilla/5.0:...
[kvcache] insert key=prefix:UserMeta:session=xyz987 ttl=60 shards=12
[kvcache] evict key=prefix:UserMeta:session=old123 cause=shard_full
```
Key example shows long header string included.

Support Bot: Customer says latency affected their internal SLA; they've temporarily throttled requests. Ticket updated.

Mike H: Repro steps (quick): spin up local runtime with small cache shard size (shard_capacity=512), send 10k unique prefixes (simulate user header noise) at 100rps, measure p95. I can share script later.

Sean L: Short-term mitigation ideas: 1) Normalize/truncate header-derived keys on the ingress path (strip long user-agent and session IDs) 2) Temporarily increase per-shard capacity or raise global cache budget 3) Enable warmup drip to avoid mass misses 4) Fallback to smaller model or disable prefix caching for noisy customers.

Alicia (runtime): Agreed. For immediate rollback, can we revert v2.14.3 canary? Is the deploy the root cause or just enabling the path?

DeployBot: Canary rollback available for us-east-1. Manual approval required.

Luis Ops: I'm going to patch a runtime hotfix to add a defensive prefix normalizer that applies canonicalization rules: remove session tokens, truncate UA to 32 chars, hash the rest. Patch will log normalized examples.

Mike H: Meanwhile I'll open a temporary global policy to cap prefix key length at 128 bytes and set a per-customer prefix-rate limiter for cache insert ops. That should reduce eviction churn.

Alicia (runtime): OK do that. Also set KV_WARMUP_DRIP_RATE to 0.2 for the affected cluster so warmup inserts are throttled and don't spike eviction. Example config: 
```
clusters.us-east1.kv_cache:
  shard_capacity: 2048
  prefix_key_max_len: 128
  prefix_normalizer: enabled
  warmup_drip_rate: 0.2
```

Sean L: After changes, we should run the repro script and verify: keep metrics of miss_rate, evict/sec, p95, p99, and cache_fill_ratio. Target: miss_rate drop 70% and p95 < 250ms.

Luis Ops: Patch deployed to a subset of nodes at 08:40 UTC. Observed immediate drop in insert rate and eviction rate. Miss rate decreased from 18% -> 5% in 10m; p95 back down to ~210ms, p99 ~420ms.

Alicia (runtime): Customer notified and kept throttle disabled. They confirmed improvement and resumed full traffic. I'll mark ticket as "monitoring" and ask support to hold for 24h.

Mike H: Follow-ups: 1) Add unit tests for prefix normalizer (edge cases: long UA, repeated query params) 2) Add per-shard eviction metrics and alert if > 2x baseline for 5m 3) Consider switching eviction policy: LRU -> Clock-Pro/LIRS evaluation for high-cardinality workloads 4) Docs: best practices for customers to avoid embedding high-entropy fields into prefix keys.

Support Bot: Ticket #5872 updated: customer confirmed SLA restored.

Sean L: One more item — we should add a short-term circuit-breaker so a single customer can't create >X unique prefix inserts in Y minutes. That will stop future cardio bursts while we build more robust normalization.

Alicia (runtime): Agreed. I'll open a follow-up RFC for runtime-level prefix hygiene and an ops runbook for cache-thrash incidents. Thanks everyone. :thumbsup:
